Support centre

Help Guide

Simple steps for everyday staff tasks.

01

Start here

Use the sidebar to open Dashboard, Attendance, Roster, Calendar, or Vendors. If you are unsure where to begin, Dashboard gives you a quick overview of today’s activity.

02

Clock in for work

Open Attendance, enter your four-digit PIN, then press Clock in. Keep the page open until the configured attendance time has passed. Your icon will then appear on the Nepali calendar. Use Break when you pause and Clock out when your shift ends.

My icon is not showing

Check that you selected Clock in and remain active. The admin chooses whether icons appear instantly, after seconds, or after minutes. Ask an admin if the record needs a manual correction.

03

Read the calendar

The large Nepali number is the main date. The smaller number is the Gregorian reference date. Green staff icons show attendance. Admins can click a date to manually select or clear staff icons when a correction is needed.

04

Use the roster

Open Roster to see weekly assignments. Staff can review the published schedule. Admins can create drafts, add shifts, use templates, move assignments, and publish the finished week.

05

Use the vendor ledger

Open Vendors and choose a vendor tab. Each main row is one bill or invoice. Click a row to expand its products, then edit quantities, rates, discounts, notes, and payments. Use the filter button to find bills and Show chart only when you need the graph.

06

When you need help

Tell an admin which page you were using, what you clicked, and what you expected to happen. Do not share your PIN, password, or private business information in screenshots or support messages.

Important for every user

Dashy currently saves information in this browser. Do not clear browser storage or change browser profiles unless an admin has confirmed that important records are backed up.

System Log

Detailed technical handoff for maintainers and future AI assistants.

Keep this export private This page describes permissions, browser data, and implementation details. Never add passwords, PINs, API keys, or private business exports.

Dashy by TNH · maintainer handoff

1. Runtime and source of truth

  • Dashy is a dependency-free Vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript application for Pokhara/Nepal operations.
  • Run locally with python -m http.server 5500 --bind 127.0.0.1 , then open http://localhost:5500/index.html .
  • index.html , app.js , and the modular files under css/ are development sources. dashy.html , styles.css , and files under deploy/ are generated or synchronized outputs.
  • After source edits, run python build.py , then python build.py . The build formats HTML, bundles ten CSS modules, copies JavaScript, and copies SVG assets.
  • Do not introduce React, npm dependencies, a bundler, or a server framework. Preserve the zero-dependency browser prototype unless the project owner explicitly changes that direction.

2. Attendance data flow

  • Staff use the PIN keypad. updateAttendance("Clocked In") creates a record in attendanceLog with staffId , Kathmandu-local Gregorian date , clockInAt , and qualified: false .
  • The qualification configuration is stored under dashy-attendance-qualification-v2 as { unit: "instant" | "seconds" | "minutes", value: number } . The default is one minute.
  • qualifyAttendanceRecords() runs when calendar icons are rendered and every 15 seconds. It compares elapsed milliseconds with the configured threshold and persists qualified records.
  • calendarAttendanceIcons(date) displays qualified automatic records. A manual admin override for the same staff/date takes precedence, including explicit removal.
  • Manual date selections are stored under dashy-attendance-overrides-v1 . Admin-only controls are client-gated by isAdmin ; production must enforce authorization server-side.
  • Changing the threshold affects records that are still unqualified. Records already marked qualified remain qualified.

3. Calendar and locale rules

  • The calendar is BS-first and uses verified year data for supported years 2080–2086. Gregorian dates are secondary reference labels.
  • Date conversion uses Asia/Kathmandu . Do not replace this with the browser’s local timezone.
  • Nepali numerals are produced by nepaliDigits() . Date cells carry data-calendar-date for admin editing and use a faint green hover state.

4. Vendors and retention

  • Vendor state is stored under dashy-vendors-v2 . One visible ledger row represents one invoice; product lines are nested in items[] .
  • Bill items calculate quantity × rate − discount. Bills also support notes, payments, filters, sorting, expandable rows, totals, and a chart below the ledger.
  • Vendor colors are editable and drive the active tab styling. Ledger column widths are resizable without admin access and persist under dashy-vendor-column-widths-v1 .
  • applyVendorRetention() limits bill history to the latest three months when vendor data is saved.

5. Staff, roster, and user management

  • Staff profiles and live statuses are stored under dashy-staff-attendance-v3 . User Management is the authoritative admin surface for profile name, role, PIN, icon, and account controls.
  • Roster drafts, templates, and published weeks use separate browser-local keys. Keep weekly Sunday–Saturday behavior and existing drag/drop patterns intact.
  • Do not move staff profile editing back into Attendance; the duplicate control was intentionally removed.

6. Storage and security boundaries

  • localStorage is device/browser-local, not a shared database. A different browser profile or cleared site data will not see the same records.
  • sessionStorage holds the current admin session. The client-side admin gate is suitable only for this prototype and is not a production authorization boundary.
  • Never log or export passwords, PINs, secrets, or private ledger contents. Avoid adding sensitive values to toasts, copied guides, or committed source.
  • When changing storage schemas, add a migration or compatibility path. Do not silently discard existing records.

7. Safe change and verification checklist

  1. Read PROJECT_CONTEXT.md and the relevant modular CSS file before editing.
  2. Search for existing keys, render functions, event delegation, and build patterns before adding new logic.
  3. Make source changes first; regenerate outputs with python build.py and python build.py .
  4. Run node --check app.js and git diff --check .
  5. Smoke-test the affected page at port 5500, including admin and signed-out behavior where relevant.
  6. Review generated files and git status --short before committing.

8. Known prototype limitations

  • There is no server-side database, multi-user synchronization, or real authorization layer in this repository.
  • Automatic attendance qualification depends on the browser timer and periodic refresh; manual admin overrides exist for corrections.
  • Supported BS conversion years are bounded. Do not silently guess dates outside the verified tables.
  • Generated deployment files must remain synchronized with development sources before publishing.
